subject: Post-demo: POC monitoring playbook, success criteria & owners
messages:
From: Sophie Tanner <sophie.tanner@finserv.io>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 17:08:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo recap: Observability & success criteria for POC

Rishi —

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier today. Team liked the latency profile and the KV cache explanation. Per our internal alignment, we want to capture the POC success criteria and the observability requirements so we can move forward quickly with procurement. High-level asks below — could you confirm Redwood can provide these (and how) in the POC?

Success criteria (what our product team will measure):
- Latency: p95 <= 250ms for generation requests up to ~512 tokens under our baseline concurrency (expected peak 20 RPS).
- Error rate: end-to-end errors < 0.5% (including model & infra errors).
- Throughput: sustain 15–20 req/s for 30m window without degradation.
- Cost target: target average per-token cost such that our projected monthly spend stays within budget (we'll share expected volume).
- Quality gate: for NPS-style evaluation, top-1 relevance/acceptance >= 85% on our holdout prompt set.

Observability & telemetry (required for evaluation):
- Dashboards: latency p50/p95/p99, request volume, error rate, tokens per request, cost per token, KV cache hit rate, model variant breakdown.
- Tracing: end-to-end traces tied to request IDs (we use OpenTelemetry); ability to export traces to our APM / OTLP collector.
- Logs: structured request/response logs (redact PII) with export to our S3 or BigQuery export.
- Alerts: simple alert rules for spike in error rate and latency degradation.
- Retention: token-level logs retained >= 30 days; aggregate metrics >= 90 days.

Operational asks:
- A proposed timeline for a 3-week POC with milestones and owner names.
- A telemetry template or dashboard we can use to evaluate (preferably a starter Grafana dashboard or LookerStudio file).
- Clarify what level of access/data we will get in the Private vs Dedicated options (for audit/procurement).

Procurement note: our procurement lead (Michael Ortega) will need the SOW and any security artifacts (SOC 2 basics) to start the contracting thread once we agree scope.

I've attached our internal POC success criteria spreadsheet for reference.

Thanks — look forward to the plan.

Best,
Sophie
Sophie Tanner
Director, Platform Engineering
FinServ.io

Attachment: FinServ_POC_SuccessCriteria.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Tanner <sophie.tanner@finserv.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 09:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: Observability & success criteria for POC

Sophie —

Appreciate the clear list and spreadsheet — this is exactly what we need to scope the POC. See a proposed POC monitoring playbook and ownership below. Happy to adjust after you review.

High-level POC plan (3-week):
- Week 0 (onboarding w/ infra & creds): account access, sample prompts, traffic profile, and logging/export config (owners: Marissa + FinServ infra). Kickoff call scheduled in week0.
- Week 1 (baseline collection): run baseline traffic, capture metrics and traces, validate dashboard instrumentation. (owner: Stephanie)
- Week 2 (stress & scenarios): run peak traffic scenarios and real-world prompt set; validate p95/p99 and errors; enable caching/quantization tests. (owners: Stephanie + Rishi)
- Week 3 (analysis & handoff): finalize dashboards, provide export of logs/traces, cost analysis, and go/no-go recommendation. (owner: Marissa)

Deliverables we will provide during POC:
- Starter observability bundle: Grafana dashboard JSON, Prometheus/OTLP mapping, and a LookerStudio token/cost dashboard (attached: Redwood_Observability_Template.pdf).
- Tracing: OTLP-compatible traces; we can ship traces to your collector or provide an exported trace bundle.
- Logs: structured logs export via S3 (we'll provide a presigned path) or BigQuery export — whichever you prefer.
- Cost model: token-level costing and example runbooks for reducing unit cost (batching / cache profiles).
- Mutual action plan (shared doc link) with milestone dates and acceptance criteria.

Suggested owners on Redwood side:
- Marissa Cole — POC lead / onboarding / business outcomes (marissa_cole@redwood.ai)
- Stephanie Nguyen — observability instrumentation, dashboards, traces (stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai)
- Rishi Malhotra — commercial point / escalation / procurement coordination (rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai)

Next steps (proposed):
1) Confirm that the success criteria in your spreadsheet map 1:1 to the acceptance criteria above.
2) Michael (procurement): we can share a short SOW and SOC 2 summary; would you prefer DocuSign or a shared PDF first?
3) Book a 60-min kickoff on Jan 22 to finalize the telemetry exports and to collect sample prompt traffic.

I've attached a starter observability template and a proposed mutual action plan doc. Marissa — can you own the kickoff scheduling and the initial onboarding checklist? Stephanie — can you draft the Grafana starter and the OTLP config by Jan 19?

Thanks — will follow up with calendar invites and the HubSpot deal link.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_Observability_Template.pdf (pdf); redwood_poc_mutual_action_plan.docx (docx)

Related: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/FS-2026-0014
